researcher_notes: OPUS REDO PASS. Blind independent re-extraction of the 4 Hikrobot files in Datasheets/AGV_AMR/Analysed/ (3 unique + 1 byte-identical duplicate). No sonnet-era findings consulted. 3 unique files → 5 products: 1 existing Forklift AGV (F3-1500, conflict), 2 NEW STU-series tote robots, and 2 pallet-handling robots from the 'QF' flyer (1 new, 1 existing). MAJOR CAVEAT ON ONE FILE: 'QF Pallet-handling Mobile Robot_Flyer_2024 Cemat_eng.pdf' has a BROKEN TEXT LAYER — its embedded subset fonts carry no ToUnicode map, so pdfplumber/pdfminer return scrambled characters. PDF page rendering is unavailable in this environment (pdftoppm/poppler not installed), so the file was recovered by solving the character substitution as a cipher using in-document cribs. Everything extracted from that file is marked and should be verified against a rendered page before import. Scope discipline: F3-1500 extracted against '*' + 'Logistics:AGV' + 'Logistics:AGV:Forklift'; the STU and QF products against '*' + 'Logistics:AGV' + 'Logistics:AGV:AMR'.

products.notes: CONFLICTS (existing DB values NOT overwritten): (1) max_speed DB=2.1 m/s vs datasheet 1.5 m/s — source: p.2 table row 'Running Speed 1.5/1.2m/s' AND p.1 key feature 'max. running speed 1.5m/s'. The flyer states 1.5 twice and explicitly calls it the maximum, so 2.1 is not supported by anything in this document. (2) vehicle_width DB=870 mm vs datasheet 863 mm — source: p.2, 'Dimension (Length*Width*Height) 1632*863*1986mm'. The DB's length (1632) matches this row exactly, so only the width digit diverges — consistent with a rounding rather than a different variant. (3) load_detection DB='Camera/Vision' vs datasheet 'Pallet recognition laser' (p.2 diagram callout) → 'Laser/LiDAR profiling'. The p.1 claim that it identifies 'black, stainless steel and other special pallets' actively argues for laser over vision. NOT MAPPED / KO FIELD NOT STATED — lifting_height: the flyer never states a lift height. Its 'Fork Height/Width/Length 60/175/1230mm' row (p.2) gives fork GEOMETRY (60 mm fork thickness, 175 mm fork width, 1230 mm fork length), not a lift stroke, and 'Applicable Scenarios' are all ground-level ('Lineside carrying', 'Ground Storage'). The DB's lifting_height=200 is neither confirmed nor contradicted by this document. min_total_height CAVEAT: 1986 mm is the only height given and the flyer does not qualify it as mast-collapsed; AP0 defines min_total_height as 'lowest overall vehicle height (mast collapsed)'. Recorded, flagged. NOT MAPPED — no AP0 field: 'Load Center Distance 600mm'; 'Fork Height/Width/Length 60/175/1230mm'; 'Fork Distance 680mm'; 'Emergency stop buttons on both sides'; 'Large panels in-position detection'; 'Body surround bumper strip'; 'Low Obstacle Detection: can effectively detect low obstacles such as forks of manual forklift' (p.1). WRONG-SCOPE FIELD AVOIDED: p.1 states 'Flexible movement: forward moving, backward moving, arc moving, rotate in place', which would map to rotation_capable — but rotation_capable exists only in 'Logistics:AGV:AMR' scope and this is a Forklift AGV, so it was not written. LEFT NULL DELIBERATELY: navigation_type (the flyer never names a navigation technology — DB has 'Natural Feature (SLAM)', unsupported here); infrastructure_free; battery_type; operating temperatures; IP rating; min_aisle_width (DB has 2100; no aisle or roadway width appears anywhere in this flyer). SCOPE BUG IN EXISTING DB ROW (pre-existing): this product is product_type='Forklift AGV' but carries route_type and route_programming (scope 'Logistics:AGV:Tugger') and workflow_capability, grid_required, picking_mechanism (scope 'Logistics:AGV:AMR'). Also fleet_management_system is stored as 'Proprietary (RCS 2000)', which is not an AP0 allowed value ('Proprietary' / 'Open API' / 'VDA 5050 compatible' / 'Third-party WMS native') — the same malformed pattern appears on the Q7-1000D and Q7-1500D rows.

products.notes: NEW PRODUCT — no STU-series or CTU product exists in the DB for Hikrobot. PRODUCT_TYPE JUDGEMENT (flagged): classified as 'Mobile AMR' by analogy with the DB's existing tote-to-person robots (Geek+ RoboShuttle RS8-DA / RS11-DA / P40 are all Mobile AMR). It is a rack-climbing container-transfer robot operating in a fixed roadway, which is arguably closer to an ASRS shuttle than to a free-roaming floor AMR — worth a Tech Lead sanity check, since product_type is a hard K.O. PLAUSIBILITY FLAGS (both recorded verbatim, neither is a read error): (a) max_payload = 30 kg is far below config/plausibility.json's required_max_payload floor of 100 kg — but this is a single-tote handler, so 30–50 kg is genuinely correct and the plausibility floor is simply tuned for pallet-class vehicles. (b) max_speed = 3.0 m/s exceeds this project's plausibility guidance (up to ~2.5 m/s even in automated zones) — but the STU runs inside an enclosed rack roadway with no human access, where 3 m/s is credible, and the flyer states it twice (p.1 headline and p.2 table). NOT MAPPED — no AP0 field: 'Max. Lifting Speed (m/s) 2'; 'Applicable Tote Dimension (L × W × H) 600*400*300 / 650*450*300'; 'Power Supply Method  Slide Touch/Battery'; 'Roadway Safety Linkage  Standard'; 'Sound and Light Alarm  Standard'; 'Noise/dB(A) ≤70'; p.1 claims 'Increase efficiency by more than 100% of single-unit stereoscopic warehouse', 'Multiple STUs can be deployed in parallel in a single roadway', 'Expandable to multi-layer combinations for ultra-high storage', 'Multiple actuators to support multi-deep, high-density storage', 'Modular design, the main components can be quickly disassembled for maintenance'. LEFT NULL DELIBERATELY: battery_type ('Slide Touch/Battery' names a power-SUPPLY method, not a cell chemistry); grid_required (AP0's NULL RULE explicitly forbids inferring it from 'racking' or 'shelving', and the flyer describes conventional 'box cross-beam racks', not an AutoStore-style grid); vehicle_length / vehicle_width / max_payload of the carried tote / IP rating / humidity — none stated. 'Support 24h continuous operation' (p.1) was NOT mapped to autonomous_charging: the flyer attributes it to 'A variety of energy options', not to unattended charging.

products.notes: *** READ FIRST — THIS PRODUCT WAS RECOVERED FROM A BROKEN TEXT LAYER AND NEEDS HUMAN VERIFICATION BEFORE IMPORT. *** The source file 'QF Pallet-handling Mobile Robot_Flyer_2024 Cemat_eng.pdf' embeds five subset fonts (all prefixed VBJISM+) with NO ToUnicode CMap, so both pdfplumber and pdfminer return scrambled characters (the title extracts as '!"#$%&&'()*%+,&-+.#/01-&'#2010('). PDF page rendering is unavailable in this environment (pdftoppm/poppler not installed), so the file could not simply be read as an image. It was instead decoded by solving the encoding as a monoalphabetic substitution, using in-document cribs — the filename gave the title plaintext ('QF Pallet-handling Mobile Robot'), which anchored the heading fonts, and 'Applicable Pallet Entry Height (mm)' / 'Rated Load (kg)' / '(ISO6780: 2003)' / '360° protection' / 'increased by 25%' anchored the body font and its digits. The decode is self-consistent and produces fluent English throughout, but at least four different subset encodings are in play and each was solved independently, so individual glyphs remain fallible. PRODUCT NAME UNCERTAINTY: the two model cells decode as a 3-character prefix + '-600D' and + '-1000D'. The prefix decodes to 'Q7' under the table-heading font's map, which matches the DB's existing 'Hikrobot Q7-1000D' naming — but the flyer's TITLE calls the family 'QF', and the prefix cell is in a different subset font than any crib could independently verify. Recorded as 'Q7-600D' to match the DB family convention; a reviewer should confirm whether the correct name is 'Q7-600D' or 'QF-600D'. STRONG CORROBORATION that the decode is right: the sibling model's decoded figures (1000 kg rated load, 1800 mm/s speed) match the DB's existing 'Hikrobot Q7-1000D' row EXACTLY (max_payload=1000, max_speed=1.8) — that row was almost certainly derived from this same flyer, which independently validates the digit map. UNRESOLVED GLYPH: the vehicle height in 'Dimension (L*W*H)(mm) 1250*1200*1?0' contains the one digit glyph that appears nowhere else in the document, so it could not be pinned down (it is either 4 or 9, i.e. 140 mm or 190 mm). No AP0 field was written from it — the AMR-scope min_ground_clearance would have been the candidate, and it is a KO field, so guessing was not acceptable. INTERNALLY ODD ROW (flagged, conservative value used): 'Rated Running Speed (Empty/Rated Load) (mm/s)  1800/2000' states the LOADED speed (2000) as higher than the EMPTY speed (1800), which is backwards. Either the label's order is reversed or one figure is a source error. 1.8 m/s was recorded as the conservative reading, matching what the DB already holds for the sibling model. NOT MAPPED — AP0 SCOPE GAP (recurring this session): p.2 states 'Roadway Width (mm)  ≥1800', which is an explicit aisle-width requirement — but min_aisle_width exists only in 'Logistics:AGV:Forklift' and 'Logistics:AGV:Tugger' scope, and this product is a Mobile AMR. Value recorded here in prose only. NOT MAPPED — no AP0 field: 'Applicable Pallet Entry Height (mm) 100-130'; 'Applicable Pallet Inner Width (mm) ≤215'; 'Applicable Pallet Outer Width (mm) 665-1000'; 'Applicable Pallet Length (mm) 600-1500'; 'Drive Method  Differential drive'; 'Ground Roller Docking Height (mm) ≤200'; 'Charging Time (h) ≤1.5' (this is a charging DURATION and would fit AP0's charge_time, but charge_time's unit is MINUTES — ≤1.5 h = ≤90 min; recorded as 90 would be defensible, but since '≤' makes it an upper bound of unclear precision on an already-uncertain decode, it was left out and is noted here instead). PRODUCT_TYPE JUDGEMENT (flagged): recorded as 'Mobile AMR' to match the DB's existing Q7-1000D classification and because p.1 describes it as an LMR (latent mobile robot) chassis. But it carries FMR forks and directly handles pallets, so the same Forklift-AGV-vs-Mobile-AMR question raised for the MiR1200 Pallet Jack applies here too. Other unmapped p.2 bullets: 'Extension modules and assemblies: supports rapid delivery and convenient operation'; 'Compared with traditional forklift, it supports extremely narrow roadway picking and putaway with the moving speed increased by 25% to increase reservoir capacity'; 'Supports various safety protection plans to realize 360° protection'; and the closing note 'The above parameters are standard products, according to the actual handling carrier, the whole robot size support customization.'

The two fields the DB already holds are confirmed exactly by this flyer: max_payload=1000 (p.2 'Rated Load (kg)', second model column) and max_speed=1.8 (p.2 'Rated Running Speed (Empty/Rated Load) (mm/s) 1800/2000' → 1800 mm/s = 1.8 m/s). This exact match is itself the strongest evidence that the cipher decode of this file is correct (see the Q7-600D entry for the full decoding caveat, which applies equally here).
